decision: made an admin password change clear the lock and outstanding reset codes
why: the administrator setting a password is the rescue path for a locked account, and an old mailed code must not outlive the password it was meant to replace

decision: gave every JT808 downlink its own serial and paired the 0x0001 answer by it
why: the plan's Appendix B postponed this because at the time nothing could be matched; the terminal answer already carries the serial of the frame it answers, so pairing needs no new protocol work, only an encoder that stops writing 0

decision: kept the serial of a command that is encoded again instead of taking a new one
why: a row that is recovered from pending after a restart must still match the answer the device sends for the frame it was queued with

decision: left the custom payload unnumbered because the caller already built the whole frame
why: numbering a frame this server did not build would rename a serial the caller embedded and could pair an answer with the wrong row

decision: put the queue and the retransmitter in gateway.Dispatcher instead of the REST handler
why: the answer path, the reconnect and the REST write all change the same state, and one owner is the only way the three cannot disagree

decision: answered an offline device with 202 queued:true instead of 409
why: the command is now worth keeping, so refusing it made the caller retry what the server could have held

decision: made a full queue a 429 that also marks the row failed
why: a queue that silently drops work is worse than a refusal the caller can see and retry

decision: bounded an unsent command with a queue ttl and a written one with the attempt count
why: waiting for a device and waiting for an answer are different waits, and a single deadline would either drop live commands or hold dead ones

decision: accepted duplicate delivery after a MarkCommandSent failure rather than risk losing the command
why: that window leaves the row pending, and the reconnect path re-encodes pending rows; a duplicate the device can dedupe beats a command nobody ever sent

decision: retired the queue entry before the store update in AcknowledgeCommand
why: the store is the authority on which row ends, and a stale entry would be retransmitted for a command that is already closed

decision: never dropped a device queue object
why: an empty queue is a few dozen bytes and deleting one raced with an enqueue that already held the pointer, which would have lost a command

decision: deleted old command rows by done_at for finished rows and created_at for the rest
why: a row that never ended has no done_at, and leaving those alone is exactly how the table grows without bound
